findings.description: The migrated local type declares availability `days: string[]`, but the source of truth (Prisma `Availability.days Int[]`, trpc list.handler returning raw prisma rows) is number[]. findings.failureMode: Type-check of @calcom/atoms fails at getScheduleListItemData(schedule) call; published type contract for schedule availability days is wrong (string[] vs actual number[]).
findings.title: GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn declares days as string[] but API/Prisma return number[]

findings.description: The replacement GetAvailableSlotsResponse declares `fromUser?: { id: string; ... }` while the server contract it replaces (IGetAvailableSlots slots with IFromUser) has `id: number`. `useAvailableSlots` result is passed as the `schedule` prop to BookerComponent (BookerPlatformWrapper.tsx:570) whose type is `useScheduleForEventReturnType` with fromUser.id: number, making the assignment ill-typed; published .d.ts also misdescribes OOO fromUser.id, so consumers using it as a string crash at runtime.
findings.failureMode: Type incompatibility between useAvailableSlots data and BookerProps.schedule; wrong published type for fromUser.id.
findings.title: SlotInfo.fromUser.id typed string but server IFromUser.id is number

findings.description: The deleted trpc type was `userIds?: number[]` (and all slot user-id types in packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts are number[]). findings.description: Unlike DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and the existing FlowRunStateTriggerFields (both switch to `trigger.after` when posture is Proactive), this component always binds the status select to `trigger.expect`. With posture "Stays in" (Proactive) and status "Not Ready", the produced trigger is {posture: Proactive, expect: ["prefect.work-pool.not-ready"], after: undefined} — per the server, Proactive triggers fire on the *absence* of expected events, so this fires when the pool does NOT emit not-ready, the inverse of "stays not-ready". Fix: derive the field name from posture like the sibling components.
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-pool status automation is created with inverted semantics (fires when the selected status event is absent instead of "stays in" that status)
findings.title: WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields writes to trigger.expect even when posture is Proactive

findings.description: Same defect as the work-pool component but a separate site needing its own patch: the status select always binds `trigger.expect`, while DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and FlowRunStateTriggerFields switch to `trigger.after` when posture is Proactive. A Proactive ("Stays in") work-queue trigger gets expect=[selected status], after=undefined, which per server semantics fires on the absence of that status event — inverted behavior.
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-queue status automation is created with inverted semantics
findings.title: WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields writes to trigger.expect even when posture is Proactive

findings.description: `String.split("\n")` always returns at least one element, so `lines.length > 0` is always true and the `undefined` branch is dead. Clearing the textarea stores `expect: [""]` (passes the zod schema `z.array(z.string()).optional()`), and a trailing newline adds "" entries. The resulting automation has an empty-string expected event and, for the empty case, silently never fires instead of expect being unset ("any event"). Fix: filter empty lines and pass undefined when none remain, e.g. `const lines = e.target.value.split("\n").filter(Boolean); field.onChange(lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined)`.
findings.failureMode: Emptying the textarea yields expect=[""] — an automation that never fires — instead of clearing the field
findings.title: Custom trigger textarea can never clear expect; empty/blank lines produce empty-string events

findings.description: This is the only threshold handler using `parseInt(e.target.value)`; deployment, work-queue, custom, and flow-run-state all use `Number(...)`. `parseInt("1e3")` returns 1 (Number returns 1000), silently storing threshold 1 for a user who typed 1e3; `parseInt("")` yields NaN which zod rejects with a confusing "expected number, received nan" instead of the min-1 message the other forms produce.
findings.failureMode: Exponential-notation input silently stores wrong threshold (1 instead of 1000); cleared field stores NaN
findings.title: Work-pool threshold uses parseInt while all sibling components use Number

findings.failureMode: Type errors no longer fail build/validation, allowing runtime type crashes to ship; direct violation of mandate requiring strict mode and a diff-visible weakening of enforcement

Same defect in work-queue-status-trigger-fields.tsx line 36.
findings.failureMode: User creating a "work pool stays in <status>" automation gets a trigger with inverted semantics (fires when status event is absent rather than persists)
findings.title: Work pool proactive trigger writes status to trigger.expect instead of trigger.after

findings.description: WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields hardcodes name="trigger.expect" regardless of posture, unlike FlowRunStateTriggerFields/DeploymentStatusTriggerFields which use "trigger.after" when Proactive. findings.description: `e.target.value.split("\n")` always returns at least one element ("".split("\n") === [""]), so `lines.length > 0 ? lines : undefined` never yields undefined and blank/empty lines are not filtered. findings.title: Custom trigger empty textarea stores [""] because split always yields non-empty array

findings.description: prepare_tools returns crate::Result<PathBuf> and calls write_and_make_executable(..)? at four sites. crate::Error has no From<FileWriteError> impl (verified: only #[from] derive variants and one From<BundleType> in settings.rs), so the ? conversion fails; tauri-bundler does not compile on Linux (mod linux is cfg(target_os = "linux"), so the break hits exactly the platform where AppImage bundling runs).

findings.description: template_renderer.py line 38: `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` lets None through, so `render_template` (declared `-> str`) returns `str | None`. Consequences: (1) `make type-check` fails: basedpyright reports `template_renderer.py:40:16 - error: Type "str | None" is not assignable to return type "str" (reportReturnType)` — a deterministic CI/build gate failure introduced by this new file; (2) at runtime, an executor result lacking the "result" key makes render_template return None and TemplateTransformNode._run raises an uncaught TypeError at `len(rendered)` instead of returning FAILED (verified by execution). Single fix: raise TemplateRenderError whenever `rendered` is not a str (drop `is not None and`).
findings.failureMode: make type-check (basedpyright, required by repo mandate 1) fails on the new file; and with an executor result missing "result", the node crashes with unhandled TypeError instead of a graceful FAILED result.
findings.title: None-passthrough in render_template breaks basedpyright type-check and can crash _run

findings.description: `rendered = result.get("result")` followed by a guard that explicitly lets None through means render_template returns `str | None` while annotated `-> str`. Verified: `make type-check` (basedpyright 1.31.0 strict) fails with reportReturnType at line 40 on this exact file. At runtime, if the executor's response mapping lacks "result", `_run` calls `len(None)` and raises an uncaught TypeError instead of returning a FAILED node result.
findings.failureMode: Repository type-check gate (make type-check / basedpyright strict) fails on the new file; runtime None result crashes the node with TypeError.
findings.title: render_template can return None despite `-> str`; fails basedpyright and crashes _run

findings.description: `rendered = result.get("result")` followed by a guard that explicitly lets None through means render_template returns `str | None` while annotated `-> str`. Verified: `make type-check` (basedpyright 1.31.0 strict) fails with reportReturnType at line 40 on this exact file. At runtime, if the executor's response mapping lacks "result", `_run` calls `len(None)` and raises an uncaught TypeError instead of returning a FAILED node result.
findings.failureMode: Repository type-check gate (make type-check / basedpyright strict) fails on the new file; runtime None result crashes the node with TypeError.
findings.title: render_template can return None despite `-> str`; fails basedpyright and crashes _run

findings.description: pytest collects zero tests from this directory (`*_spec.py` doesn't match default patterns, no python_files override), and the module cannot even import (ModuleNotFoundError: core.workflow.graph_engine.entities.graph). The 700+ new test lines also pass `graph=mock_graph` to the new __init__ (which has no `graph` param) and config without id/data, so they'd TypeError/ValueError if ever run. The claimed unit coverage of the renderer abstraction is illusory.
findings.failureMode: Zero verification of the new renderer wiring; regressions go undetected despite PR claiming updated tests.
findings.title: PR's renderer tests never execute (dead spec file); would fail if collected
